full_text_en:
Agricultural Bank of China Trust and Investment Company v. China Light Industry Raw Materials General Company — dispute over loan guarantee contract (appeal)

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Agricultural Bank of China Trust and Investment Company.

Legal representative: Cao Jiren, General Manager.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Derong and Zhang Yali, attorneys from Shihua Law Firm.

Appellee (defendant at first instance): China Light Industry Raw Materials General Company.

Legal representative: Jiang Zhenyu, Deputy General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Tong Qiang, attorney from Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

The appellant, Agricultural Bank of China Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as the Investment Company), dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance rendered by Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court in the dispute over a loan guarantee contract with the appellee, China Light Industry Raw Materials General Company (hereinafter referred to as the Material Company), appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. The Investment Company alleged on appeal that: The Investment Company is a financial institution approved by the People's Bank of China to engage in trust lending operations and is authorized to grant trust loans. Even if the entrusted loan contract in this case were in fact a trust loan, it should still be a valid loan contract. The Material Company assumed joint and several liability for repayment of this loan, and when the borrower, Suzhou Jiaxiang Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiaxiang Company), failed to perform its obligations under the contract, the Investment Company was entitled to demand that the Material Company make payment on its behalf. The Investment Company requested that the court of second instance revoke the original judgment. The Material Company argued in its defense that: The entrusted loan contract in this case violated the law. By requiring the Material Company to provide a guarantee for such a contract, the Investment Company had committed malicious fraud against the Material Company. Therefore, the Material Company should not bear the guarantee liability.

The Beijing High People's Court found upon trial that: On April 1, 1993, a third party, Beijing Chongwen District Guoti Imported Auto Parts Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Guoti Business Department), entered into an Entrusted Loan Agreement (No. (93) 006) with the appellant Investment Company. The agreement stipulated that Guoti Business Department would entrust the Investment Company to issue loans totaling RMB 50 million from April 6, 1993 to July 6, 1993; upon maturity of the entrusted loan funds, the Investment Company would repay the principal and interest in a lump sum to Guoti Business Department; the objects, interest rates, and purposes of the entrusted loans were not expressly stipulated. After execution of the agreement, Guoti Business Department deposited RMB 50 million with the Investment Company on April 6, and the Investment Company issued a large-sum fixed deposit certificate for a term of three months, maturing on July 6, with a monthly interest rate of 8.1‰. On July 10, Guoti Business Department withdrew RMB 40 million of the deposit principal and RMB 124,900 in deposit interest, and on July 13, it withdrew the remaining RMB 10 million of the deposit principal and RMB 8,100 in interest. At this point, the entire RMB 50 million deposit and deposit interest of Guoti Business Department had been fully withdrawn.

On April 12, 1993, Jiaxiang Company submitted a loan application to the Investment Company and on the same day signed an Entrusted Loan Contract (No. (93) Nong Yin Xin Wei Zi 008), which stipulated: The Investment Company, upon entrustment under Agreement No. (93) 006, would issue an entrusted loan to Jiaxiang Company in the amount of RMB 5 million for short-term working capital turnover; the term was two months, from April 13, 1993 to June 13, 1993; the monthly interest rate was 18‰; interest was to be repaid together with principal upon maturity; if Jiaxiang Company failed to pay interest on time, a late payment penalty of 0.05% per day on the overdue amount and overdue days would be imposed; if the loan was not used for the specified purpose, a penalty interest of 50% would be added; if the principal was not repaid on time, an additional interest of 20% would be added. The contract also stipulated that the Investment Company agreed that the Material Company would act as the economic guarantor for Jiaxiang Company, and the guarantor bore joint and several liability for repayment; if the borrower failed to repay the loan principal, interest, and penalties on time, the guarantor undertook to unconditionally repay all amounts owed on behalf of the borrower within ten days of receiving notice from the Investment Company. The Investment Company, Jiaxiang Company, and the Material Company all affixed their seals and signed the contract. On the same day, the Material Company also issued an irrevocable guarantee letter to the Investment Company, undertaking a guarantee amount of RMB 5 million, and stipulating that if the borrower failed to repay all or part of the loan principal, interest, and related expenses in accordance with the contract, the guarantor would unconditionally repay the loan principal, interest, and expenses owed by the borrower within seven days of receiving written notice from the Investment Company. On April 13, Jiaxiang Company and the Investment Company jointly signed an IOU, the contents of which regarding the borrowing unit, loan amount, loan term, and loan interest rate were consistent with the contents of the Entrusted Loan Contract No. 008. On April 13, the Investment Company disbursed RMB 4,906,400 to Jiaxiang Company. Jiaxiang Company repaid RMB 1 million to the Investment Company on July 17 of the same year, and thereafter made no further repayment of principal or interest. The Material Company also failed to perform its guarantee obligations. After repeated demands by the Investment Company yielded no results, the Investment Company filed a lawsuit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, requesting that the Material Company perform its guarantee obligations to repay the principal and interest and compensate for losses.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held that: The Entrusted Loan Agreement No. (93) 006 contained nothing regarding the entrusted loan beyond the statement that Guoti Business Department entrusted RMB 50 million for lending. The instrument issued by the Investment Company for the RMB 50 million was a fixed deposit certificate for a lump-sum deposit with a fixed term; upon maturity, the Investment Company had returned the full RMB 50 million deposit and deposit interest to Guoti Business Department. Furthermore, the loan amount under Contract No. (93) Nong Yin Xin Wei Zi 008 was inconsistent with the loan amount under Agreement No. (93) 006. Therefore, the civil relationship between the Investment Company and Jiaxiang Company should be a trust loan relationship, and the Entrusted Loan Contract No. 008 signed by both parties should be invalid. The Investment Company's claim that it issued the loan upon entrustment by Guoti Business Department and had signed an entrusted loan contract with Jiaxiang Company could not be upheld. The guarantee contract relationship between the Material Company and the Investment Company was ancillary to the invalid Contract No. 008. As the principal contract was invalid, the guarantee contract should also be confirmed as invalid, and the Material Company should no longer bear joint and several guarantee liability to the Investment Company for Jiaxiang Company's debts. The Investment Company should exercise its rights against the borrower, Jiaxiang Company, in accordance with the law. Accordingly, on November 8, 1996, the court rendered judgment: Dismissing the plaintiff Investment Company's claims. Court costs of RMB 50,707 and litigation preservation fees of RMB 40,320 were to be borne by the Investment Company.

The Beijing High People's Court held that: Although Contract No. 008 signed between the appellant Investment Company and the borrower Jiaxiang Company was in form an entrusted loan contract but was in substance a trust loan contract, it was concluded on the basis of voluntariness, equality, mutual benefit, and consensus after negotiation. The rights and obligations of each party were clearly defined. Except for the interest rate clause, which was slightly high and violated regulations, the other clauses did not contravene national laws or regulations and complied with the provisions of Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and therefore the contract should be valid. The appellee Material Company signed and affixed its seal on the contract as guarantor and issued an irrevocable guarantee letter to the Investment Company. The clauses regarding the guaranteed amount, term, and assumption of joint and several guarantee liability reflected the true and clear intentions of the parties, and their content was lawful, having been accepted by the Investment Company. This complied with Article 8 of the Regulations on Loan Contracts, and therefore the guarantee contract should also be valid. Article 90 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Lawful lending relationships are protected by law." The parties should strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contract. When Jiaxiang Company failed to repay the borrowed funds and interest on time, and upon demand by the Investment Company, the Material Company still failed to perform its obligation to repay on behalf of the borrower as stipulated, it had constituted a breach of contract. Under these circumstances, in accordance with Article 111 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the Investment Company was entitled to demand that the Material Company perform its joint and several repayment obligation and was also entitled to demand that the Material Company compensate for losses. At the time of signing the contract, the Investment Company did not intentionally deceive or conceal the true situation from the other party. On the contrary, the loan object, amount, term, including interest rate and guarantee liability, were specified very clearly in the contract. Whether the name of the contract was trust loan or entrusted loan did not alter the guarantor's guarantee liability, nor did it involve any fraud against the guarantor. The Material Company's defense that the discrepancy between the name and content of the contract was illegal, and that providing a guarantee for such a contract was due to fraud by the Investment Company, and therefore it should not bear guarantee liability, lacked factual and legal basis and could not be upheld. The Investment Company's appeal arguments were reasonable and should be supported, except that interest exceeding the state-prescribed interest rate for the corresponding period would not be protected. The facts found at first instance were clear, but the determination that the contract was invalid and the exoneration of the guarantor from guarantee liability were improper, and the judgment dismissing the Investment Company's claims was erroneous and should be amended. Accordingly, in accordance with subparagraph (2) of Article 153(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Beijing High People's Court rendered judgment on April 2, 1997:

1. Reversing the civil judgment (1996) Yi Zhong Chu Zi No. 591 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court;

2. Suzhou Jiaxiang Real Estate Co., Ltd. still owes Agricultural Bank of China Trust and Investment Company a loan principal of RMB 3,906,400, together with interest and overdue penalty interest (from April 13, 1993 to June 13, 1993, interest at the People's Bank of China benchmark lending rate for the corresponding period on RMB 4,906,400; from June 14, 1993 to July 17, 1993, overdue interest at the People's Bank of China overdue penalty rate for the corresponding period; from July 18, 1993 until the date of payment, overdue interest at the People's Bank of China overdue penalty rate for the corresponding period on RMB 3,906,400). China Light Industry Raw Materials General Company shall bear joint and several liability.

3. The above amounts shall be paid within fifteen days from the date of service of this judgment. In the event of late payment, proceedings shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The court costs of first instance and second instance, RMB 50,707 each, and the litigation preservation fee of first instance of RMB 40,320, shall be borne by the appellee, China Light Industry Raw Materials General Company. Since the appellant, Agricultural Bank of China Trust and Investment Company, has advanced these amounts, they shall be paid to the appellant together with the above sums.
